approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored molecules. It samples high-ranked breeding parents, recombines connected fragments and applies local mutations and occasional successive mutations; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled. Stable identity checks form a fresh surplus pool. An accepted-only Gaussian process represents molecules by counts of local Morgan environments and uses generalized Tanimoto similarity. Its correlated posterior score draws allocate the next evaluations, and accepted offspring update the full prediction archive and the bounded breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove environment multiplicity from the predictor by replacing each cached count vector with binary presence in exactly the same molecular vocabulary. Keep the shared kernel equation, fitting settings and correlated allocation rule. This is a reverse control on the current exchange-free Parent: earlier count variants improved the mean on an exchange-enabled search, while narrowing intervals and worsening coverage, and they repeated the same trajectories. No evaluated same-Parent child in this brief has tested the representation removal. The pending correlation and mean-only controls retain count features and change allocation instead. This experiment asks whether count information still supports endpoint search, with a predicted loss when it is removed; any replay of an older binary search will be identified explicitly.

hypothesis: Remove Morgan environment multiplicity from the shared posterior representation by replacing each inherited count vector c with binary presence 1[c > 0] for every training, pool and next-fit feature use, while retaining the generalized Tanimoto implementation and all fitting, graph-generation and correlated-allocation rules.

finding_summary.headline: Removing environment counts lowers the matched mean by 0.051296 and reproduces the earlier binary search
finding_summary.insights: The isolated reverse control supports a positive contribution of environment multiplicity in the current exchange-free composition. It changes both fitted means and covariance, so the experiment does not assign the gain specifically to calibrated uncertainty. More structural variety is also insufficient: binary selection yields 2,267 typed and 1,546 generic cores versus 1,851 and 1,118 under counts, yet strict local parent beats fall from 629 to 565 and incumbent gains from 258 to 218. Molecular evidence preserves the useful conventional ketone and aminoaryl-dione gains alongside reactive environments, repeated large assemblies and destructive fragments; no universal size or chemistry rule explains the score loss. The fifteen trajectories and all shared non-timing decisions exactly reproduce the earlier binary ancestor. That establishes provenance and rules out treating the replay as new independent evidence; the current matched Parent comparison remains the contribution test. Which changes in similarity, means and covariance mediate the useful search behavior remains open.
finding_summary.results: Every active feature is binary under extensive repeated-environment exposure, and all 435 fitted pools change their posterior relative to counts on the same inputs. The retained correlated draws, graph operations and accepted feedback reconstruct correctly. Mean final score falls from 0.595670 to 0.544374, a paired loss of 0.051296 against the registered 0.002 scale. All seed macros decline: 0.077877, 0.002003 and 0.074008. Twelve task-seed endpoints decline; zaleplon_mpo improves on seed 0, while deco_hop and sitagliptin_mpo improve on seed 1. On the actual binary stream, latent 1.96-SD coverage is 79.75% versus 73.52% for a passive count model using the same earlier labels and scored molecules. Their MSEs are 0.016600/0.009873. Binary error is higher in all fifteen task-seed cells, while its coverage is lower for median_2 on every seed despite the aggregate increase. These diagnostics answer a different question from endpoint search utility.

molecular.headline: Compact ketone and aminoaryl-dione leaders coexist with reactive heterocycles, repeated large assemblies and low-scoring fragments
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were present and read. Every task has 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The brief reports complete Child evaluation and complete profile-matched pairing with code Parent n-62daf219c70a, with no profile-mismatched seeds. The Parent comparisons below therefore use the complete published current-profile panel. This report describes chemistry and its observed score associations; it does not judge activation or attribute individual structural changes to the feature-representation intervention. The output remains rich in rings and aromatic frameworks: ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9736 to 0.9943, and aromatic-string incidence 0.9414 to 0.9885. These counters measure presence in a molecule, not perceived ring count, aromatic-atom fraction or useful scaffold diversity. The molecules include compact annulated ketones, nitrogen/sulfur-containing spiro and bridged systems, linked heteroaromatic carbonyl assemblies, aryl-containing basic amines, medium/large nitrogen-carbonyl rings and fluorinated fused diones. Families differ across seeds, but leaders often remain close relatives within a seed, supporting moderate overall structural diversity. Some conspicuous leaders have comparatively conventional local chemistry: the ketone/fluoropyridyl family and an aminomethyl/fluoroalkyl aryl-dione family improve their matched Parent scores without N-F bonds. The strongest aryl-amine examples also use ordinary carbon-bound halogens. These counterexamples prevent a claim that reactive heteroatom-halogen chemistry is unavoidable. Nevertheless, other leaders contain N-F/N-Cl, peroxide-halogen chains, cyanates, aldehydes, chloromethyl ethers or crowded nitrogen/sulfur bridges. Large repeated aryl/dione assemblies and tiny poor-scoring fragments occur alongside the compact families. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak; the visible conventional examples do not validate the complete set. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 for all tasks, despite protonatable amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres. Heavy-atom sizes below were counted from the cited trajectory SMILES tokens; geometry, synthesis and physical properties were not validated. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, and some final proposals are poor fragments or truncated analogues despite a better retained incumbent. Parent statements use its published trajectories; cited_smiles contains only current molecules allowed by the digest or trusted citation paths.

Configurations and accessible geometry of annulated and sulfur/nitrogen-rich centres are unresolved; lower scoring unrelated seeds do not prove that a particular missing bond or atom is required.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Observed in n-e00db808bbb4 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task, with complete current-profile Parent n-62daf219c70a. The environment gap previously recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c persists through N-halogen, oxygen-oxygen-halogen, cyanate, aldehyde and chloromethyl-ether chemistry. Counterexamples are especially important here: a compact ketone family and a conventional aminoaryl-dione family improve matched Parent scores without N-F, and the strongest aryl-amine examples use carbon-bound halogens. Thus reactivity is conditional on local environment and is not unavoidable for useful output.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain conventional bond environments while exploring useful aromatic and polar arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need plausible local alternatives preserving feedback-supported functional-group relationships, while distinguishing ordinary carbon-bound halogens, amides, ethers and amines from reactive bond patterns. Preserve and explore the demonstrated conventional alternatives. The evidence does not prove that a blanket filter improves score or attribute any specific liability to the feature representation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e00db808bbb4 under complete paired Search conditions with n-62daf219c70a, continuing the context/coverage gap first recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful molecular context while controlling repeated elaboration and destructive simplification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local feedback to test independent connectivities and simplifications that preserve useful aromatic, carbonyl and basic-region relationships, rather than treating repeated motifs or fewer atoms as sufficient. The missing capability is consistent preservation of functional context, not an inability to form rings or large molecules. No fixed size cutoff, repetition ban or component-level causal claim follows from this chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e00db808bbb4 on the supplied complete Search panel and profile, compared with n-62daf219c70a. Leaders contain nitrogen/sulfur bridges, spirocycles, carbon centres attached to several nitrogens, larger nitrogen-carbonyl rings and compact fused diones. Ring text remains prevalent throughout. The earlier geometry concern from n-c55c3d520a2c persists in changed structures, while a conventional aminoaryl-dione and a recognizable diazaspirocycle are counterexamples to a uniformly implausible output. The Parent's particular cyclic-cumulene leader is not a property of the current best family.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently establish geometric and synthetic feasibility for crowded annulations, aminal centres and larger nitrogen rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Topology changes need environment-sensitive assessment of ring connectivity, unsaturation, aminal stability and accessible conformations, with alternative structures preserving learned useful arrangements. Ring counts and aromatic text cannot establish feasibility. Preserve conventional small and spiro rings where appropriate; this evidence does not establish that all unusual topology is impossible or that geometric filtering necessarily raises reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e00db808bbb4 across all supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task, continuing the identity gap recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and Parent n-62daf219c70a. Every task has stereocentre-string and formal-charge-string incidence 0.0, although substituted saturated rings, spiro/bridged structures and aminoalkyl centres can have stereochemical distinctions. Clear primary, secondary and tertiary amines remain present, so neutral strings do not establish a lack of protonatable chemistry. The comparatively conventional leading dione does not remove the issue from the other generated families.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves relevant stereochemical and molecular-state identity unspecified after producing saturated and heteroatom-rich structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve relevant stereochemistry, with separate assessment of protonation, tautomerism and imine/alkene configuration. Distinguish achiral or configurationally labile structures from those needing stable stereoisomer assignment. These observations establish incomplete chemical identity, not a measured state-dependent score penalty or proof that adding charge or enumeration improves the objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

activation_observables.measurement: Reconstruct the unchanged generator raw count vector c on each logged training, pool and previous-emission query identity, and verify every actually used feature row is exactly 1[c>0], with identical support, dimension, cache identity/order and float64 device interface. Actual bins above one must fall to zero everywhere; row totals must equal the number of nonzero bins and maximum entries must be at most one. Count raw repeated-bin opportunities and rows unchanged by binarization separately for training, pools and probes; distinguish repeated sparse environment identifiers from extra multiplicity caused by folding collisions when inspecting structural exposure. The Parent has repeated training bins in all 435 logged fits, but no fixed Child exposure count is assumed. Exact support/value tests permit no mismatch. Raw counts reconstructed offline are passive controls and must not re-enter fitting or selection.
activation_observables.name: Binary feature use under repeated-environment exposure

activation_observables.measurement: For each actual chronological archive/pool state, independently reconstruct binary and passive count models using the identical accepted labels/order, normalization, noise and bounded jitter law. Verify the unchanged generalized kernel reduces exactly to binary Tanimoto on binary inputs, with unit nonempty diagonals and inherited empty-vector conventions. Report differences in train/train, train/query and query/query similarities, score-unit means and SDs, and standardized full conditional covariance using a declared 1e-10 float64 reconstruction tolerance. Require actual nondegenerate kernel/posterior displacement where the representation changes effective relationships; raw repeated counts alone do not prove a changed posterior. Separate coincident predictions, constant-label or empty-vector cases and numerical failures. Measure the historical expectation that removing counts often increases SD exposure, without requiring a universal sign or claiming calibrated uncertainty. Reconstruct next-fit probes on identical emitted identities, separating standardized covariance contraction from changing empirical score scale. No new score or alternative search is supplied by these same-state comparisons.
activation_observables.name: Fixed-input kernel and posterior displacement from count removal

activation_observables.measurement: Inspect the complete source diff: only cache-miss binarization and truthful passive fit labels may change. Reconstruct every successful draw and masked argmax from the actual binary posterior, full factor including its recorded jitter, original score scale and recorded standard normals. Confirm the single inherited random-array call, masks, first-index ties and identity-bound predictions remain; successful choices must still maximize the correlated sampled rows and are not forced into posterior-mean order or independent residuals. With the same raw normals, separately replay the passive count model using its own masks and report changed positions/sets; these alternate choices remain unscored. On common pre-divergence inputs compare retained calculations, and after divergence audit each actual state on its own history. Join every emission through pending identity, finite accepted feedback, full archive, survivor state, later breeding and next-fit probe; confirm unchanged graph rules, disabled exchanges, crossover/ordinary mutations, stable identity, duplicates, exact announced batches and objective-local restarts. Check potential correspondence to n-213e85380e04 by comparing actual binary support/kernel and generation/allocation behavior, then trajectories and non-timing shared receipts if formal data become available. Report any first divergence or exact reproduction; source similarity or equal endpoint alone is insufficient. Reproduced historical trajectories add no independent seeds and do not replace the current Parent comparator.
activation_observables.name: Retained correlated allocation and accepted-only feedback with changed representations

activation_observables.measurement: Join prospective selected binary predictions to accepted scores and compare with a passive count model built on exactly the same earlier accepted state. Report MSE against both that same-state comparator and the archive-mean baseline, within-batch prediction/score rank relation, latent interval width and one/1.96-SD coverage by task and seed. If observation-noise-inclusive intervals are reported, label them separately and use the unchanged noise; no interval result selects a model or changes an online parameter. Wider intervals or lower error do not establish endpoint benefit. Also report accepted batch maxima, strict best-parent beats, child-minus-best-parent scores, incumbent gains, survivor admissions and later reuse, selected typed/generic Murcko-core coverage with an explicit acyclic convention, feature-equivalence ties and molecule-size distributions. Separate identical-state representation comparisons from complete adaptive stream differences, distinguish counts from resolution of exact feature aliases, and do not assign unobserved oracle outcomes to passive choices.
activation_observables.name: Predictive coverage and search behavior on actually scored emissions

finding_summary.insights: The isolated reverse control supports a positive contribution of environment multiplicity in the current exchange-free composition. It changes both fitted means and covariance, so the experiment does not assign the gain specifically to calibrated uncertainty. More structural variety is also insufficient: binary selection yields 2,267 typed and 1,546 generic cores versus 1,851 and 1,118 under counts, yet strict local parent beats fall from 629 to 565 and incumbent gains from 258 to 218. Molecular evidence preserves the useful conventional ketone and aminoaryl-dione gains alongside reactive environments, repeated large assemblies and destructive fragments; no universal size or chemistry rule explains the score loss. The fifteen trajectories and all shared non-timing decisions exactly reproduce the earlier binary ancestor. That establishes provenance and rules out treating the replay as new independent evidence; the current matched Parent comparison remains the contribution test. Which changes in similarity, means and covariance mediate the useful search behavior remains open.
finding_summary.results: Every active feature is binary under extensive repeated-environment exposure, and all 435 fitted pools change their posterior relative to counts on the same inputs. The retained correlated draws, graph operations and accepted feedback reconstruct correctly. Mean final score falls from 0.595670 to 0.544374, a paired loss of 0.051296 against the registered 0.002 scale. All seed macros decline: 0.077877, 0.002003 and 0.074008. Twelve task-seed endpoints decline; zaleplon_mpo improves on seed 0, while deco_hop and sitagliptin_mpo improve on seed 1. On the actual binary stream, latent 1.96-SD coverage is 79.75% versus 73.52% for a passive count model using the same earlier labels and scored molecules. Their MSEs are 0.016600/0.009873. Binary error is higher in all fifteen task-seed cells, while its coverage is lower for median_2 on every seed despite the aggregate increase. These diagnostics answer a different question from endpoint search utility.

molecular_assessment.headline: Compact ketone and aminoaryl-dione leaders coexist with reactive heterocycles, repeated large assemblies and low-scoring fragments
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were present and read. Every task has 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The brief reports complete Child evaluation and complete profile-matched pairing with code Parent n-62daf219c70a, with no profile-mismatched seeds. The Parent comparisons below therefore use the complete published current-profile panel. This report describes chemistry and its observed score associations; it does not judge activation or attribute individual structural changes to the feature-representation intervention. The output remains rich in rings and aromatic frameworks: ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9736 to 0.9943, and aromatic-string incidence 0.9414 to 0.9885. These counters measure presence in a molecule, not perceived ring count, aromatic-atom fraction or useful scaffold diversity. The molecules include compact annulated ketones, nitrogen/sulfur-containing spiro and bridged systems, linked heteroaromatic carbonyl assemblies, aryl-containing basic amines, medium/large nitrogen-carbonyl rings and fluorinated fused diones. Families differ across seeds, but leaders often remain close relatives within a seed, supporting moderate overall structural diversity. Some conspicuous leaders have comparatively conventional local chemistry: the ketone/fluoropyridyl family and an aminomethyl/fluoroalkyl aryl-dione family improve their matched Parent scores without N-F bonds. The strongest aryl-amine examples also use ordinary carbon-bound halogens. These counterexamples prevent a claim that reactive heteroatom-halogen chemistry is unavoidable. Nevertheless, other leaders contain N-F/N-Cl, peroxide-halogen chains, cyanates, aldehydes, chloromethyl ethers or crowded nitrogen/sulfur bridges. Large repeated aryl/dione assemblies and tiny poor-scoring fragments occur alongside the compact families. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak; the visible conventional examples do not validate the complete set. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 for all tasks, despite protonatable amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres. Heavy-atom sizes below were counted from the cited trajectory SMILES tokens; geometry, synthesis and physical properties were not validated. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, and some final proposals are poor fragments or truncated analogues despite a better retained incumbent.
